title: Psalms Chapter 108 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 108 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 108 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 108.

questions.question: According to Psalms 108:1, what is fixed in the psalmist's heart?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:1 states, 'O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.'

questions.question: What musical instruments are mentioned to awake in Psalms 108:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:2 says, 'Awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early.'

questions.question: In Psalms 108:3, among whom does the psalmist say he will praise the LORD?
options: Among the people and among the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Among the people and among the nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:3 states, 'I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 108:4, how is God's mercy described?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:4 says, 'For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to be, according to Psalms 108:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:5 states, 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth;'

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 108:6, the psalmist asks for deliverance by God's right hand.
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:6 says, 'That thy beloved may be delivered: save with thy right hand, and answer me.'

questions.question: Who does the psalmist say is his lawgiver in Psalms 108:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:8 states, 'Judah is my lawgiver;'

questions.question: According to Psalms 108:7, what will the psalmist do with Shechem?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:7 says, 'I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth.'

questions.question: In Psalms 108:9, what is Moab called?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:9 states, 'Moab is my washpot;'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 108:10 asks who will lead the psalmist into the strong city.
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:10 says, 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?'.

questions.question: Who does the psalmist question about casting them off in Psalms 108:11?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:11 states, 'Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts?'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 108:12, help from man is described as vain.
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:12 says, 'Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 108:13, through whom shall the psalmist do valiantly?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:13 states, 'Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies.'

questions.question: In which order does the psalmist mention these actions in Psalms 108? Choose the first action mentioned.
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:1 mentions first 'I will sing and give praise,' before other actions like awakening instruments or dividing Shechem.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 108:5 calls for God’s glory to be above all the earth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:5 states, 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth;'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 108 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 108 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 108:6, what does the psalmist ask God to do for His beloved?
options: Deliver them and save with His right hand
Bless them with wealth and prosperity
Grant them long life and peace
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver them and save with His right hand
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:6 specifically asks God to deliver His beloved and save with His right hand. This shows the psalmist’s trust in God’s power to rescue and protect. This is consistent with the victorious tone in verses 7-9 where God’s authority over territories is declared.

questions.question: How does Psalms 108:7 demonstrate confidence in God's promise and holiness?
options: By rejoicing and dividing Shechem and the valley of Succoth
By asking God to send rain upon the fields
By fasting and praying for mercy
By building an altar for sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: By rejoicing and dividing Shechem and the valley of Succoth
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows confidence in God's promise as the psalmist proclaims rejoicing that God has spoken in holiness, and declares he will divide Shechem and mete out the valley of Succoth, indicating trust in God's guidance and blessing over territorial victories (verses 8-9 support God's sovereignty over lands).

questions.question: Which territories are claimed as belonging to the psalmist in Psalms 108:8?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 clearly states that Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Judah are the psalmist’s, with Judah called the lawgiver. This expresses God's grant of authority and blessing over these tribes, tying to the victorious theme in verse 9.

questions.question: What symbolic act does the psalmist declare over Edom in Psalms 108:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:9 says, 'over Edom will I cast out my shoe,' a symbolic act of claiming authority or conquest, similar to customs of claiming land. This illustrates triumph, consistent with the psalmist's declaration of victory over Philistia and ownership of other lands (verses 8-9).

questions.question: What question does the psalmist ask in Psalms 108:10 regarding entering the strong city and Edom?
options: Who will bring me into the strong city and who will lead me into Edom?
When will the enemies be defeated and the city restored?
How can we find peace with Edom and the strong city?
Why has God forsaken us and left the city vulnerable?
questions.correctAnswer: Who will bring me into the strong city and who will lead me into Edom?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 directly asks, 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?' reflecting the psalmist’s dependence on God for guidance and victory, which is answered in the following verses (11-13) emphasizing God's help over human aid.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 108:11-12, what does the psalmist say about human help compared to God's help?
options: Human help is vain, and God must go forth with our hosts
Human help is sufficient, but God's help is superior
Human help is reliable, and God supports it
Human help is better than God’s intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Human help is vain, and God must go forth with our hosts
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 state that human help is vain and question if God, who has cast them off, will go with their hosts, implying the psalmist's recognition that only God’s intervention can bring victory, emphasizing faith and dependence on God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 108:13 describe the outcome through God's help?
options: We shall do valiantly and tread down our enemies
We shall be defeated but learn humility
We shall find peace and rest from battle
We shall conquer the heavens and the earth
questions.correctAnswer: We shall do valiantly and tread down our enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 13 declares confidently that through God we shall do valiantly, for He will tread down our enemies, summarizing the psalmist’s trust in God’s power to grant victory and courage in battle, consistent with the preceding verses about God’s help and triumph.

questions.question: What does Psalms 108:7-8 teach about God’s holiness and His granting of authority?
options: God speaks in holiness and grants territories like Shechem, Gilead, and Judah
God demands sacrifices for holiness and chooses kings
God hides His plans but blesses the faithful
God punishes nations for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: God speaks in holiness and grants territories like Shechem, Gilead, and Judah
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 combine the declaration that God has spoken in holiness with the psalmist's rejoicing in dividing Shechem and owning Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Judah, showing God’s holiness is connected to His granting of authority and blessing.

questions.question: How does Psalms 108:6-7 connect the request for deliverance with the response of rejoicing and territorial division?
options: Deliverance by God leads to rejoicing and rightful division of land
Rejoicing causes deliverance and territorial gain
Territorial division is unrelated to deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance by God leads to rejoicing and rightful division of land
questions.explanation: Verse 6 petitions God for deliverance of the beloved, while verse 7 responds with rejoicing and the intention to divide Shechem and the valley of Succoth, indicating that God’s deliverance results in joyful rightful possession of land, reflecting faith in God’s promises.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is highlighted by the psalmist’s prayer in Psalms 108:11-12 about God’s presence in battle?
options: Humility and dependence on God rather than human strength
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and dependence on God rather than human strength
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 show the psalmist humbly acknowledging that human help is vain and pleading for God’s presence with their hosts, teaching believers to depend on God rather than their own strength or human aid in challenges.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 108:9 states that the psalmist will triumph over Philistia and claim Moab as a washpot.
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:9 explicitly says, 'Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; over Philistia will I triumph,' indicating triumph over Philistia and ownership over Moab as a washpot, symbolizing subjugation.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 108:10, the psalmist confidently states that he alone will enter the strong city and lead into Edom without God's help.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 asks, 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?' showing the psalmist’s dependence on God’s leadership rather than claiming to do it alone, which is reinforced by subsequent verses asking for God's help.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 108:13 teaches that through God’s help, believers will do valiantly and overcome their enemies.
questions.explanation: Verse 13 affirms that 'Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies,' emphasizing that victory and courage come through reliance on God.

questions.question: What practical lesson about prayer and trust can a believer learn from Psalms 108:6-13?
options: Pray for deliverance and trust God’s power to lead and conquer
Rely mainly on human help and prepare for battle
Avoid praying for enemies and focus on personal gain
Seek peace through compromise with adversaries
questions.correctAnswer: Pray for deliverance and trust God’s power to lead and conquer
questions.explanation: Verses 6-13 teach believers to pray earnestly for deliverance and rely wholly on God’s power to lead them and grant victory, as human help is insufficient (verses 11-13).

questions.question: Based on Psalms 108:7-9, how does the psalmist’s confidence in God’s promise influence his view of leadership and territory?
options: It affirms God’s sovereignty over tribes and gives confidence to act justly
It encourages taking land by force without God’s guidance
It suggests ignoring leadership and focusing on personal success
It demands isolation from other nations
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God’s sovereignty over tribes and gives confidence to act justly
questions.explanation: The psalmist’s declaration of owning territories and dividing land (verses 7-9) reflects confidence in God’s sovereignty and holiness, which legitimizes his leadership and actions, encouraging just and faithful stewardship.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 108 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 108.

questions.question: According to Psalms 108:11, what does the psalmist ask God regarding His presence with the hosts?
options: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts?
Shall we not be delivered from our enemies?
Do you hear the cries of the faithful?
questions.correctAnswer: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts?
questions.explanation: The psalmist questions God's seeming abandonment and pleads for His presence to go forth with the hosts, as stated in Psalms 108:11.

questions.question: What reason does Psalms 108:12 give for asking God for help?
options: Because vain is the help of man
questions.correctAnswer: Because vain is the help of man
questions.explanation: The verse states that human help is vain, emphasizing the need for divine assistance (Psalms 108:12).

questions.question: What outcome does Psalms 108:13 predict through God's help?
options: We shall do valiantly and tread down our enemies
We shall build a strong city
We shall be delivered by human strength
questions.correctAnswer: We shall do valiantly and tread down our enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:13 clearly affirms that through God, the people will act valiantly and defeat their enemies.

questions.question: Which ancient territories are mentioned as belonging to the psalmist in Psalms 108:8?
questions.explanation: The verse lists these specific territories as belonging to the psalmist, symbolizing Israel's tribal lands (Psalms 108:8).

questions.question: What is the literary device prominently used in Psalms 108:4 where mercy and truth are described as reaching beyond the heavens and clouds?
questions.explanation: The description of mercy 'above the heavens' and truth reaching 'unto the clouds' is an intentional exaggeration to emphasize God's greatness, a hyperbole (Psalms 108:4).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also emphasizes that help from man is vain, paralleling the theme in Psalms 108:12?
questions.explanation: Psalm 127:1 similarly states that without the LORD's help, human efforts are in vain, paralleling Psalms 108:12's theme of reliance on God.

questions.question: In Psalms 108:9, what object is used metaphorically to express dominion over Moab?
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares 'Moab is my washpot,' a metaphor showing subjugation and contempt (Psalms 108:9).

questions.question: The psalmist in Psalms 108:7 speaks of dividing Shechem and meting out the valley of Succoth. What is the significance of this in the context of Israel's history?
options: It symbolizes the restoration of Israel's territorial inheritance
It refers to a future building project
It predicts the destruction of these regions
It is a call for exile from these places
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the restoration of Israel's territorial inheritance
questions.explanation: The verse reflects God’s promise to restore Israel’s lands, recalling tribal allotments and conquest (Psalms 108:7).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 108:10 questions who will bring the psalmist into the strong city and lead him into Edom.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly asks who will lead into the strong city and Edom, showing dependence on God's guidance (Psalms 108:10).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 108:5 declares that God's glory is only above the heavens but not over the earth.
questions.explanation: The verse states God's glory is above the heavens and above all the earth, not limited to the heavens (Psalms 108:5).

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'right hand' in Psalms 108:6 symbolizes what in biblical context?
questions.explanation: In Hebrew scripture, 'right hand' often signifies God's power to save and deliver, as seen in Psalms 108:6.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of triumph over enemies through God as expressed in Psalms 108:13?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:37 declares believers are more than conquerors through Christ, echoing the victorious theme of Psalms 108:13.

questions.question: What theme from Psalms 108 is fulfilled in the Messianic prophecy found in Isaiah 53:5?
options: Deliverance through suffering and victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance through suffering and victory over enemies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 speaks of suffering that brings healing and victory, paralleling Psalms 108’s theme of God’s deliverance (Psalms 108:13, Isaiah 53:5).

questions.question: In Psalms 108:3, the psalmist intends to praise God among which groups?
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares praise both among the people and the nations, showing universal worship (Psalms 108:3).

questions.question: Which literary structure is suggested by the repetition and parallelism between Psalms 108:11-13, emphasizing God’s role in battle?
questions.explanation: The repeated invocation of God’s presence and help at the beginning and end of the passage forms an inclusio framing the prayer for victory (Psalms 108:11-13).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 108 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 108 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 108:1 indicate about David's attitude towards God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:1 states, 'O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.' This indicates David's determined and unwavering commitment to worship God.

questions.question: In Psalms 108:3, who does David intend to praise among the people?
questions.explanation: David declares in Psalms 108:3, 'I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations,' indicating his desire to exalt God in front of all nations.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 108:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:4 states, 'For thy mercy is great above the heavens,' clearly emphasizing God's attribute of mercy as immense and transcendent.

questions.question: What request does David make to God in Psalms 108:6?
options: To save with His left hand
questions.explanation: In Psalms 108:6, David asks, 'save with thy right hand, and answer me,' indicating a plea for divine assistance and intervention.

questions.question: What does David express in Psalms 108:7 regarding God's communication?
options: God has spoken in His holiness
questions.correctAnswer: God has spoken in His holiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:7 states, 'God hath spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice,' which acknowledges God's clear and authoritative communication.

questions.question: Which region is mentioned as belonging to David in Psalms 108:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:8 states, 'Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine,' indicating David's claim over these territories.

questions.question: How does David express his confidence in God's help in Psalms 108:12?
options: Through man we shall be saved
questions.explanation: In Psalms 108:12, David says, 'Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man,' expressing his reliance on God over human assistance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 108:13 reveal about David's confidence in God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:13 states, 'Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies,' showcasing David's faith in God's power to deliver victory.

questions.question: What insight does Psalms 108:9 provide about David's attitude towards Moab?
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:9 declares, 'Moab is my washpot,' which indicates David's view of Moab as a place of contempt and subjugation.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 convey about God's nature?
options: God is indifferent to our needs
God's mercy and glory lead to deliverance
God does not care for His people
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and glory lead to deliverance
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 together highlight that 'Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens' and 'that thy beloved may be delivered,' emphasizing the connection between God's mercy and His glory in delivering His people.

questions.question: What does Psalms 108:11 imply about God's relationship with Israel?
options: He will go forth with them
questions.correctAnswer: He will go forth with them
questions.explanation: In Psalms 108:11, David asks, 'Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts?' This suggests David's hope that God will restore His presence with Israel.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I will divide Shechem' in Psalms 108:7 indicate about David's intentions?
questions.explanation: David's statement 'I will divide Shechem' in Psalms 108:7 indicates his intention to conquer and claim territory as part of God's promise to him.

questions.question: What does the reference to 'Edom' in Psalms 108:10 signify in David's military context?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 108:10, David asks, 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?' which indicates Edom as a target for military action.

questions.question: How does Psalms 108 relate to the broader narrative of redemption in Scripture?
options: It shows God's sovereignty in Israel's history
It focuses only on David's reign
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's sovereignty in Israel's history
questions.explanation: Psalms 108 reflects God's sovereignty and faithfulness in David's victories and the establishment of Israel, which is integral to the redemptive narrative.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's help is unreliable. What does Psalms 108:12-13 actually teach?
options: God's help is essential and effective
God does not help His people
questions.correctAnswer: God's help is essential and effective
questions.explanation: Psalms 108:12-13 emphasizes that 'Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man. Through God we shall do valiantly,' affirming the necessity and effectiveness of divine assistance.
